title: If Norway Went Down the Drain
section_path: If Norway Went Down the Drain
section_path_text: If Norway Went Down the Drain
summary:
If Norway Went Down the Drain
Norway's oil workers threatened to strike this past week potentially knocking between 720,000 to 2.5 million barrels per day out of the current exports of 3.2 million bpd. Norway is the world's fourth largest crude oil exporter behind Saudi Arabia, Russia, and Iran. The Norwegian government was successful in ending the week-long strike by negotiating a settlement between employers, which include several oil majors, and workers.

children.title: Exports
children.summary: Consumption Longer Voyage, More Ships, Higher Rates The upshot of a cessation of exports from Norway would have to be a substitution by Saudi Arabian crude since Russia is producing at maximum capacity and Venezuela and Iran are close to maximum. Such an event would not only strain Saudi Arabia, but also would drain the VLCC fleet capacity and consequently drive rates to extreme highs.

children.title: The Existing Situation
children.summary: Not all North Sea oil is destined for Europe. For Aframax tankers fixed on the spot market, most are destined for other European ports with a small number fixed to the Mediterranean.

children.title: UKC
children.summary: USA Med Suezmax tanker fixtures from the North Sea to UKC destinations have been declining, but fixtures to East Coast Canada and the United States have been expanding, which voyage-wise benefits Suezmax tanker owners.

children.title: UKC
children.summary: Canada&USA Med Asia VLCC loadings have also experienced a decline. Most spot fixtures of North Sea crude in VLCCs are to East Coast Canada and the United States with a small number to Asia as backhaul cargoes.

children.title: Canada&USA
children.summary: Asia Not An Oil Crisis, But a Tanker Crisis Saudi spare capacity is about equal to that of one major oil producer such as Venezuela, Nigeria, or the Norwegian North Sea. If two major oil producers were to cease for a sustained period of time, the paramount problem would be lack of oil availability.
